subject: Veridian POC: capacity fit walkthrough & next steps
messages:

Subject: Veridian POC: capacity fit walkthrough & next steps

Thanks again for the call today — great to meet the Veridian team. Quick recap and a few asks so we can size a clean Dedicated PO C proposal (and confirm whether we should route this to Dedicated first or start with Hosted and move to Private/VPC later).

Key points from the demo we captured:
- Primary workload: customer-facing summarization + retrieval-augmented generation for product pages.
- Target SLA: interactive latency (p50 ~ 80–120ms, p95 under 350ms) for 95% of requests; occasional background batch jobs allowed to be higher.
- Expected traffic: steady-state ~150–200 TPS, daily peaks up to ~450–500 TPS for product launches.
- Token mix: median prompt ~250 tokens, generation avg ~600 tokens (heavier on generations for long-form summaries).
- Compliance: eventual requirement for VPC/private deployment (SOC2 + custom DSRs). POC can start on Dedicated if that speeds time-to-eval.

Please confirm the numbers above or correct anything I got wrong. Action items we need from you to size Dedicated correctly:
1) Confirm steady-state TPS and expected peak length in minutes (e.g., 10-min peak burst vs sustained hour-long peak).
2) Confirm % of requests that are short responses (<128 tokens) vs long-form (>512 generated tokens) — even rough breakdown helps (e.g., 60/40).
3) Any hard latency SLOs tied to SLA or enterprise contract?
4) Do you have constraints on GPU family (no H100, only A100) or absolute preference?

I've attached a short worksheet (veridian-poc-requirements.xlsx) — if you can fill the traffic shape column that will make the sizing exact.

Next steps: once we get the worksheet back, Karthik will sketch a 2-option sizing (cost-optimized and latency-optimized) and Ben will prepare a short Mutual Action Plan and PoC SOW draft. Goal: have a PoC proposal by next Tue 10/13.

Thanks — Grace

Thanks Grace — notes look right, appreciate the concise recap. Quick answers below so you can proceed with sizing.

1) Traffic shape:
- Steady-state: 180 TPS (business-as-usual daytime hours)
- Typical peak: 480 TPS for ~20 minutes during product bulletins; rare multi-hour peaks up to ~600 TPS during large launches (we'd expect to throttle some background jobs in those cases).

2) Token breakdown (rough):
- ~55% short responses (<128 tokens)
- ~30% medium (128–512 tokens)
- ~15% long-form (>512 tokens) — these are the heaviest and drive burst planning.

3) Latency SLOs: p95 < 300ms is our goal for interactive features; we can accept up to 700–800ms for long-form responses if cost tradeoffs are required.

4) GPU constraints: We do not have contractual limits on GPU vendor, but our procurement prefers predictability. If you recommend H100 for latency but show cost delta versus A100 with quantization, procurement will evaluate.

Timeline: we want to start a 4-week PoC in early Nov. We prefer Dedicated (reserved pool) for the PoC to validate isolation and throughput, with a roadmap to move to Private/VPC for production later in Q1.

I've attached an initial traffic sample export to the Drive folder (see HubSpot note) — let me know if you need the raw logs.

Best,
Sophie

Sophie — thanks for the details, that makes sizing straightforward. A quick tech sketch to help your procurement team evaluate tradeoffs.

Sizing assumptions you provided: steady 180 TPS, 20-minute peaks to ~480 TPS, token mix ~55/30/15 short/med/long, avg prompt 250 tokens, avg gen 600 tokens for long requests. Latency p95 target ~300ms.

Option A (latency-optimized, recommended for validation of p95 SLA):
- Start PoC on Dedicated with 4 x NVIDIA H100 80GB instances (multi-GPU nodes) configured with continuous batching + KV prefix caching.
- Expected sustained capacity: ~180 TPS comfortably; headroom for 480 TPS peaks with autoscaling to 6 GPUs for short bursts.
- Concurrency: plan for ~10–12 concurrent interactive streams per GPU for long-form gen; short requests multiplex higher (25–30).
- Benefits: headroom for p95 < 300ms without aggressive quantization; simpler model variants, fewer quality tradeoffs.

Option B (cost-optimized):
- 5 x NVIDIA A100 40GB with int8/4-bit quantized model path and optimized kernels (we can provide quant profiles).
- Expected sustained capacity: ~160–200 TPS with p95 near target for short/medium responses; long-form p95 may stretch to ~450–600ms depending on batch sizes.
- Concurrency: higher multiplexing per GPU (20–30 for short requests), but long-form memory pressure requires careful batching to avoid OOMs.

Operational suggestions for both options:
- Use dynamic routing: host short/latency-critical routes on the low-latency pool, and route long-form jobs to a slab with higher batching tolerance.
- Enable prefix/KV caching for repeat prompts (we saw ~18% cache hit rate on similar customers).
- Set autoscale policies keyed to 1-min and 5-min windows to handle 20-min bursts quickly.
- We recommend a small canary (1–2 GPUs) of Private/VPC config to validate networking and compliance before full prod migration.

I'll attach a quick back-of-envelope cost delta in the Drive folder; Ben can follow up with a PoC SOW and timeline. If you'd like, we can map the two options to monthly cost estimates and expected token-unit costs.

Sophie/Carlos — thanks for the quick answers and the traffic sample. Attached is a short PoC SOW draft (redwood-poc-sow-draft.pdf) + a proposed Mutual Action Plan. High-level next steps we suggest:

1) Veridian: send back the completed requirements worksheet + confirm preferred PoC start week (you mentioned early Nov).
2) Redwood: provide two sizing options (latency & cost) with monthly cost estimates and an A/B test plan for H100 vs A100 quantized.
3) Veridian: approve PoC SOW or propose edits (DocuSign link to follow once we agree on scope & term).
4) Redwood + Veridian: schedule a 60-min ops kick to validate VPC networking and logging requirements (we'll include our security lead if needed).

If PoC needs to be Dedicated from day 1, we can reserve capacity in the region you requested — confirm region and any procurement POs we should expect.

I'll drop the DocuSign link and cost spreadsheet into HubSpot and the shared Drive by EOD.

Looking forward to moving this forward — Ben
